counterfactual_missing_items: No major abnormalities observed in both lungs and heart
increase in absolute FEV1 of 250 mL, improvement rate of 24%
Past medical history included hospitalization in intensive care unit one year ago requiring mechanical ventilation for over 10 days
decisive_items: Loud and diffuse wheezing rales in both lungs
Blood gas analysis: pH 7.137, PCO2 74.7 mmHg, PO2 95.0 mmHg, SO2 94.0%, FiO2 41.0%, oxygenation index 232 mmHg
response.rationale: R4 uniquely combines chronic recurrent asthma history with acute severe exacerbation, diffuse wheezing, and type-2 respiratory acidosis (pH 7.137, PCO2 74.7 mmHg), matching status asthmaticus. R6 has severe historical PFT/ICU evidence but lacks the acute ABG and wheezing anchors, while R2/R5/R1/R3 are contradicted or incomplete.

rejected.why: Age 30, bronchodilator reversibility, asthma control scores, and eosinophilia favor asthma over COPD; no smoking or emphysema raw support.
Normal chest CT and no CF-specific raw findings directly contradict cystic fibrosis.
Only wheezing is cited; it misses acute ABG, prior ICU ventilation, and severe PFT abnormality.
Respiratory failure is the acute complication of the underlying asthma exacerbation, not the most likely primary diagnosis.
